sections.这一篇讲什么:
**Context engineering decides which tokens belong in the window at each inference.**
Anthropic's official definition: prompt engineering writes instructions; context engineering
curates and maintains the optimal set of tokens during inference — system instructions, tools, external data, message history all count.
The window is a budget, not a warehouse: stuffing more in does not mean getting more out.
We have not run hands-on tests; the mechanisms below come from official docs and papers.
sections.注意力预算与位置效应:
Anthropic calls the phenomenon context rot:
as context tokens grow, the model's ability to accurately recall information from that context declines.
The root is the transformer architecture: n tokens form n² pairwise attention relations,
and the longer the sequence, the thinner the capacity to capture them gets stretched.
Short sequences dominate training data, so models also have less experience with long-range dependencies.

The Lost in the Middle paper tested multi-document QA and key-value retrieval:
performance is highest when relevant information sits at the beginning or end,
and degrades significantly when it lands in the middle of a long context.
Explicitly long-context models behave the same way.
Takeaway: do not bury key information mid-context; a big window is not uniformly good.
sections.静态前置，动态后置:
OpenAI's prompt caching matches on prefixes:
a request first checks whether the beginning of the prompt is already cached; a hit reuses it, a miss processes everything and caches the prefix.
It activates automatically above 1024 tokens — no request changes needed.
The placement rule follows: instructions, examples, and tool definitions up front; user-specific variable content at the end.

Three details decide the hit rate:
tool definitions and their order must be exactly identical across requests;
multi-turn history is only appended to the end of the messages array, never reordered;
the `cached_tokens` field in the response reports hits, and prefixes unused for a while are evicted.
Caching is organization-scoped; the official docs state no data is stored during the process, making it eligible for zero data retention.
sections.按需检索与渐进披露:
Another way to save budget: do not pre-load data — keep lightweight identifiers.
File paths, stored queries, links; load on demand at runtime with tools.
Anthropic cites [Claude Code](../../coding/products/claude-code.md) as its example:
write targeted queries, inspect slices with head/tail, and never load whole data objects into the window.
Identifier metadata carries signal: directories, naming, and timestamps hint at purpose and relevance.
The agent explores layer by layer, keeping only what is currently needed in working memory.

The official trade-off is explicit: runtime exploration is slower than pre-computed retrieval;
without guidance the agent misuses tools, chases dead ends, and misses key information.
Hybrid strategies are common: pre-load some data for speed, leave the rest to autonomous exploration.
sections.长任务的三种手法:
When a task outgrows the window, Anthropic offers three routes:

1. Compaction: summarize history near the limit and reinitialize the window. Tune recall first, then precision; clearing old tool results is the lightest touch.
2. Structured note-taking: the agent periodically writes notes outside the window and reads them back later. Progress and dependencies survive window resets.
3. Sub-agents: each explores deeply in a clean window and returns only a distilled summary; the lead agent synthesizes.

Choose by task shape: compaction preserves conversational flow, notes suit milestone-driven iterative development,
and sub-agents suit research and analysis where parallel exploration pays off.
sections.失败模式:
1. Edge-case laundry lists: stuffing every rule into the prompt. The official advice is diverse, canonical examples instead.
2. Bloated tool sets: overlapping functionality, ambiguous choices. If a human cannot say which tool to use, the agent cannot do better.
3. Over-aggressive compaction: dropping details that look trivial now but matter later. Tune the compaction prompt on complex traces.
4. Waiting for bigger windows: the official judgment is that relevance problems persist at any size — curation cannot be skipped.

System prompts have two extremes of their own: hardcoded if-else logic is brittle, vague guidance is empty.
The official advice: start minimal, then add instructions and examples based on observed failure modes.
